content:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: API gateway (edge) returning elevated 502/504 errors. 5m error rate 16.9% (baseline ~0.2%). Detected 2023-11-02T18:17:56Z. Region: us-east-1. Pager: @ben

ben: Got the pager, joining. Can someone post quick impact numbers? :phone:

maria: seeing the same in grafana. 2xx down ~40%, latency spiking, increased upstream timeouts to origin. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat.

carla: adding context — we pushed a routing change 20m ago that increased fanout to proxy pool A (canary) during burst. Not sure if related.

ben: OK. Kai, can you snapshot the edge proxy pool health? Also collecting the first 1min of logs.

kai: running query: `sum(rate(ingress_5xx_total[1m])) by (upstream)`

kai: results: bulk of 5xx from upstreams origin-0, origin-2. origin-1 looks ok.

maria: tail from edge node e-12 shows repeated: `upstream handshake timeout` and `502 bad gateway` back to back. Sample: ```
[2023-11-02T18:16:40Z] proxy[e-12] upstream origin-0 timeout after 20s
[2023-11-02T18:16:41Z] proxy[e-12] returned 502 for req id=abc123
```

ben: This looks like upstream (origin) timeouts, not proxy code. First action: enable upstream retry+shorten timeout for the affected routes to reduce client 502s. Maria, can you flip timeout reduction and enable 1 retry?

maria: doing now — patching ingress config: `upstream_read_timeout 10s` and `proxy_next_upstream error timeout http_502` then reload.

support-bot: Noted. Creating incident ticket IN-20231102-44321 and alerting support.impact_channel.

carla: Also rolling back the routing change to pool A is prudent if it correlates. Ben, want a rollback?

ben: Yes, rollback pool A  to previous weight (80% -> 20%) and pause canary. Do that after we confirm config reload.

maria: reload done. Confirming config: `nginx -s reload` returned OK. Grafana dash shows slight dip in 502s but still high.

kai: Running `curl -I https://edge-us-east.example/v1/health` from within edge nodes: some succeed, some 502. Tracing upstream to origin-2 shows increased connection queuing and 504s reported by origin.

maria: origin-2 backend logs show GC stalls and CPU at 98% on the serving processes. Looks like an application-level overload/latency.

ben: Escalate to Eng Runtime and Origin owners. Carla, can you ping runtime-team? I'll call a quick sync if we think customers are impacted heavily. :phone:  

carla: @carla -> @dave-runtime (runtime oncall) pinged. Dave, any quick wins on origin side?

dave: Oncall here. Seeing sudden spike in request queue length and periodic worker crashes. Rolling restart of origin-2 worker pool now. Also bumping max_workers from 16 -> 24 as a short-term mitigation.

ben: Good. Maria, keep an eye on error rate after restart. Also enable temporary circuit-breaker: fail fast to 503 for overloaded origin instead of cascading 504s if restart doesn't stabilize.

maria: restart started at 18:24:10Z. Applying circuit-breaker policy to route `/v1/*` with 10% failure threshold (fail fast) — patch applied.

kai: Telemetry: 18:25Z after restart error rate dropped to ~6.5% — still above baseline but trending down. Latency median down from 950ms to 420ms.

support-bot: Incoming customer reports: 7 distinct customers reported API timeouts in last 10m. No critical enterprise support tickets yet. Notifying sales-cust-ops.

ben: Good to know. Let's classify impact: Severity P2 (partial outage with customer impact, not fully blocked). If we see >20% requests failing or high-severity customer reports, escalate to P1.

carla: Rolling back canary weight now per earlier instruction. Executing rollback to previous config.

maria: Rollback applied. Confirming traffic rebalanced to origin-1 and origin-0 more evenly. Additional headroom on origin-2 after restart.

dave: origin-2 worker pool back online, error logs subsiding. Investigating root cause — possible memory leak in latest release; collecting heap dumps. Will open a follow-up bug.

ben: For immediate mitigation, we should: 1) keep the reduced upstream timeout + 1 retry 2) keep circuit-breaker in place for 30m 3) maintain increased worker count on origin-2 for 1 hour 4) schedule postmortem once stable. Anyone object?

carla: +1

maria: +1 — monitoring thresholds set: alert if 5xx > 8% for 5m.

kai: Noted, I'll keep a watch on queue lengths and pod restarts.

support-bot: Customer impact note added to ticket IN-20231102-44321: "~6-18% error rate observed between 18:17-18:32 UTC affecting generation/chat routes in us-east-1; temporary mitigations applied; engineering investigating origin instability."

ben: I'll remain on this thread for handoff. Maria — if things keep trending down, prepare a short status update to #general and post-incident blameless timeline. If we get more reports or rate jumps, escalate to P1 and page execs.

maria: Understood. Will send status update at 18:45Z with current metrics and mitigation steps.

dave: Created internal ticket RT-5591 to track origin memory issue and heap dump analysis.

carla: Thanks team. Handoff plan: ben -> carla in 30m if stable. Ben, confirm when you want the ownership transfer.

ben: Will hand off at 18:50Z if 5xx < 4% for the preceding 10m. Otherwise I'll keep owning until stable.

maria: Current snapshot 18:36Z: 5xx 3.2% over 10m, median latency 210ms. Looks stable.

ben: Ok handing off to Carla now. I'll leave this incident in monitoring and on-call. Carla, you're point. :white_check_mark:

carla: Taking ownership. I'll coordinate the postmortem and confirm remediation timeline. Thanks all.

support-bot: Incident IN-20231102-44321 updated: status -> monitoring, owner -> carla, severity -> P2.

maria: Posting brief external status to support-cust-ops: "We observed elevated errors for certain API routes in us-east-1 earlier; mitigations applied and systems stable. We will follow up with a full incident report."

ben: Closing note: follow-ups — root cause analysis (memory leak?), improve canary gating for routing weight changes, add additional health-checks to upstream to avoid long handshake timeouts.

carla: Noted. I'll assign action items during postmortem. Good job team. :tada:
